findings.title: Local cache is populated before the store write, so a device rejected by the limit is let through on its next request
findings.body: `tagDeviceUI` calls `a.localCache.SetDefault(key, struct{}{})` before `a.anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice`. When the store returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, the error is propagated and `Anonymous.Authenticate` correctly refuses the request, but the device's cache key has already been written. On the very next request from the same `X-Grafana-Device-Id` (and for the next ~29 minutes), `tagDeviceUI` hits the cache and returns nil, so `Authenticate` succeeds and the device is served as a normal anonymous user even though it was never recorded and the limit is still exhausted. The device limit is therefore only enforced for a single request per device per cache lifetime. The cache entry must only be written after `CreateOrUpdateDevice` succeeds (or be deleted on `ErrDeviceLimitReached`).

findings.title: Count-then-insert is not atomic; concurrent new devices can exceed the configured limit
findings.body: `CreateOrUpdateDevice` runs `CountDevices` in one DB session and the insert/upsert in a separate `WithDbSession` call, with no transaction or row locking. If several previously-unseen devices authenticate concurrently (or across multiple Grafana instances, which share the table but not the local cache), each sees `count < deviceLimit` and all of them insert, so the number of active devices can exceed `device_limit` by the degree of concurrency. If the limit is meant to be a hard cap (it blocks authentication), the check and insert should be performed in a single transaction, or the insert should be made conditional in SQL.

findings.title: Unauthenticated callers can exhaust the device limit with arbitrary device IDs and lock out anonymous access for 30 days
findings.body: `X-Grafana-Device-Id` is a client-supplied header with no validation, and each distinct value creates a row in `anon_device`. With `device_limit` set, `Authenticate` now returns an error for any new device once the count is reached. An attacker can send `device_limit` requests with random header values and thereby block all legitimate new anonymous visitors; the fabricated rows stay counted for 30 days (`anonymousDeviceExpiration`) and there is no admin endpoint to delete devices (`/api/anonymous/devices` is read-only). This turns the limit into a trivial denial-of-service vector for anonymous access. At minimum the behaviour and the recovery path should be documented, and a delete/cleanup API or ID validation considered.

findings.title: Device limit is bypassed by any request that omits the X-Grafana-Device-Id header
findings.body: `TagDevice` returns nil immediately when the `X-Grafana-Device-Id` header is absent, and `Authenticate` then issues a full anonymous identity. Since the limit is only enforced inside `CreateOrUpdateDevice`, any client that does not send the header (curl, scripts, a browser with the header stripped) is never counted and is never blocked, even when the limit is reached. The new `device_limit` setting therefore cannot be relied on as an access cap; it only constrains well-behaved UI clients. This should be documented clearly for the setting, or non-UI anonymous requests should be handled explicitly when the limit is active.

findings.title: ProvideAnonDBStore now requires an int64 and ProvideAnonymousDeviceService no longer accepts an AnonStore; DI wiring must be updated
findings.body: Before this change `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` received an `anonstore.AnonStore` from dependency injection, which implies `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore` (and a `wire.Bind` for `AnonStore`) is registered in `pkg/server/wire.go`. This PR changes `ProvideAnonDBStore` to take `(db.DB, int64)` and makes the service construct the store itself, but `wire.go`/`wire_gen.go` are not in the changed file set. If the provider is still listed, wire generation fails (no provider for `int64`, or an unused-provider error); if it has been silently dropped elsewhere, any other consumer of `anonstore.AnonStore` loses its provider. The wiring changes should be included in this PR and `make gen-go`/wire regenerated.

findings.title: anonymousDeviceLimit is typed as `undefined` on GrafanaBootConfig and the backend never sends undefined
findings.body: `anonymousDeviceLimit = undefined;` without an explicit type annotation gives the class field the static type `undefined` (not `number | undefined`), so consumers of `config.anonymousDeviceLimit` cannot use it as a number without a cast even though `merge(this, defaults, options)` assigns a number at runtime. Additionally, `FrontendSettingsDTO.AnonymousDeviceLimit` is a non-`omitempty` `int64`, so the backend always serialises a number (0 when the limit is disabled) and the `| undefined` in `GrafanaConfig` never occurs in practice. Declare it as `anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined = undefined;` (matching `loginError`) or type it as `number` with a 0 default, and make the DTO/TS types agree.

findings.title: No test covers the 'update existing device when limit reached' path or the client rejecting a new device
findings.body: `TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit` only verifies that a second, new device is rejected. The new `updateDevice` branch (an already-counted device must still be refreshed when `count >= deviceLimit`, and a stale device outside the 30-day window must be rejected) is untested, as is the end-to-end behaviour in `Anonymous.Authenticate` returning an error on `ErrDeviceLimitReached` and the interaction with the local cache in `impl_test.go`. Given the limit now gates authentication, these paths should have coverage; a test for the cache interaction would have caught the bypass described for `tagDeviceUI`.
